summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes, kidney transplantation, and breast cancer treated with radiation presented with a two-week history of dry cough, fever, and fatigue, initially dismissed as viral. Due to persistent symptoms and immunocompromised status, she was admitted for further evaluation. Chest imaging revealed multifocal bronchopneumonia, and she was started on levofloxacin, with resolution of fever and improvement in symptoms. A 6 mm endobronchial nodule was incidentally noted, prompting a recommendation for follow-up CT in six weeks. Her diabetes remained difficult to control during illness, but she declined insulin dose adjustments, opting to follow up with her endocrinologist. She maintained stable renal function, remained compliant with immunosuppressants, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics with plans for outpatient monitoring.
